MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

L10·N857unmasked layer
This neuron has a very small activation range and no clear semantic selectivity — it fires weakly on the predictable continuation token of a common collocation/phrasal verb mid-sentence (e.g. "I'll **show** you", "pick **up**", "lead them on **an** exploration", "it **was** accepted"), i.e. it looks like a noisy phrase-completion neuron rather than a concept detector (with equally arbitrary verb/noun tokens like "feature", "laugh", "extracted", "place" driving it negative).

score 0.23requests for code or actions ("write a Python function", "about playability and potential with slots")
the activation arises from the pattern of a list or enumeration, specifically when the enumeration involves various classification categories or types (e.g. "class 2", "about playability and potential with slots"). L10·N5753unmasked layer
This neuron fires on function words that open a verb's object/complement — determiners, possessives, complementizers and infinitival "to" ("review **the** final invoice", "prepare **our** children", "ensure **that**", "nice **to** have") — peaking on the word right after the governing verb; it is suppressed on content nouns/quote marks and numeric-list positions.

L10·N11203unmasked layer
